1.title: The Issues Practice
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: The Issues Practice. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain the purpose of the issues practice and its relationships with the principles. Explain the purpose of the issue management approach, issue register and issue report. Define issue and its types, project baseline and change control. Describe baselines, issue resolution, change control, delegating authority for changes and the change budget. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (sixty percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Purpose
1.text: Purpose. The issues practice captures, assesses and manages issues so that they are resolved or escalated and the project stays under control. It also handles changes to the project baseline in a controlled way.

1.title: Key concepts
1.text: Key concepts. Issue. A relevant event that has happened, was not planned, and needs management action. Project baseline. The approved version of the project's products and plans used as the reference for control. Change control. The process that makes sure changes to baselines are assessed, approved and recorded.

1.title: Types of issue
1.text: Types of issue. Request for change. A proposal to change a baseline. Off-specification. Something required that is not (or will not be) provided as specified. Problem or concern. Any other matter the project manager must resolve or escalate. Business opportunity. An issue that offers a chance to improve the business case (sometimes raised as a change).

1.title: Types of issue, continued
1.text: Types of issue. The figure shows this: Issue types and where each goes: change control or direct resolution.

1.title: Types of issue, continued
1.text: Types of issue. The exact list of types in the official book. Exam tip: Risk equals might happen. Issue equals has happened. Request for change and off-specification are types of issue, not risks.

1.title: Guidance
1.text: Guidance. Baselines. Approved products and plans; changes need control. Issue resolution. Capture, assess, propose, decide, implement (the issue technique). Change control. Assess impact on cost, time, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability, then approve or reject. Delegating authority for changes. The project board may give the change authority or the project manager power to approve changes within limits. Change budget. A sum of money the board sets aside to pay for approved changes. The issue technique: capture, assess, propose, decide, implement.

1.title: Management products
1.text: Management products. Issue management approach (P I D). How issues and changes are managed on this project. Issue register (project log). A record of all issues, their status and decisions. Issue report. A detailed description of one issue (or a request for change or off-specification), with analysis and recommendation. Exam tip: Request for change and off-specification are issue types. Change control applies to changes to baselines. Exam tip: The change budget is set aside by the board to pay for approved changes.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A user asks for an extra feature after the requirements were baselined. Which type of issue is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Request for change. A proposal to change a baseline is a request for change.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) An issue has already happened. (two) An off-specification is something that is not provided as specified. (three) An issue is something that might happen. (four) A change budget is a risk allowance. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one and two. Issues have happened, and off-specifications are not as specified.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. A blank is the approved version of products and plans used as the reference for control. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Baseline. That is a baseline.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. The board sets aside money to pay for approved changes. What is it called? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Change budget. The board provides a change budget.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which management product describes one issue in detail with analysis and a recommendation? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Issue report. The issue report covers one issue in detail.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Who may be given authority to approve changes within limits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The change authority or the project manager, as delegated by the board. The board can delegate change authority within limits.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define an issue. Answer: A relevant event that has happened, was not planned and needs management action. Question two. Name the types of issue. Answer: Request for change, off-specification, problem or concern, and business opportunity. Question three. What is change control? Answer: The process that assesses, approves and records changes to baselines.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the change budget? Answer: Money set aside by the board to pay for approved changes. Question five. What does the issue register record? Answer: All issues, their status and decisions. Question six. Name the five steps of the issue technique. Answer: Capture, assess, propose, decide and implement.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Issue: has happened, unplanned, needs action. Types: request for change, off-specification, problem or concern, business opportunity. Baseline or change control: approved reference or assess, approve, record changes. Authority: change authority; change budget. Products: issue management approach, issue register, issue report.
